what: Woven polyester (Dacron) sailcloth with a resin finish: the J/22's crosscut main and jib, the Sunfish's striped sail. The white cloth carries the wear; the Sunfish's dyed bands keep their own sun fade (Livery SailFade).

boats.Sunfish: Layout 1 striped; only its white band ages by these rules

material: M_SailCloth (SAIL_CODE in scripts/make_materials.py); the boat-kit Dacron slot (BOAT_CODE surf 10) uses the same targets for furled cloth and sail bags

pattern.note: weave and panel sizes already match the real cloth (docs/sail-cloth-shading); this loop does not change them

replaces: Today's look: yellowing at the leech and head and mildew specks at the foot are fixed (the same on every sail, whatever its Age and Care); only the foot grime (dirtK) and the crinkle (ageC) follow Age/Care. A brand-new sail is already yellow and speckled, and a kept 30-year-old sail is as grimy as a half-neglected one.

wear.time: UV yellowing (whole cloth, most at the leech and head), crinkle cover and fold strength, resin loss (roughness up, sheen down), stitched repairs and sail tape
wear.dirt: foot grime from the deck, tan clay smudges where hands and the boom touch, mildew specks (foot and folds), grey dinge over the whole cloth

budget: Medium: colour and roughness math only (no new maps, no texture reads). High/Ultra: the existing crinkle and weave normals; no new maps.
tests: SailRigTests (M_SailCloth has Age/Care), BoatTextureBudget, the Mac boats gate (scripts/gate.sh --scope boats)
